messages.content: I’m starting the Nashville certification workshop plan. It’s Wednesday Oct 14 through Friday Oct 16 near Music City Center, and my husband may join for a Saturday-night extension if I stay until Sunday. Can you look at DEN flights and the official hotel block versus something nearby?
Sure. Before I rank it: are you assuming economy or main cabin, and do you want to plan for arriving Wednesday or add Tuesday as a safety buffer? Also, what block hotel and rate did they give you?

Economy is fine. I’d rather not add Tuesday unless the agenda forces it. The block is Renaissance Nashville at $249 plus tax, walkable to the workshop. If there’s an afternoon-ish flight that still gives me enough buffer, great, but don’t make the first day stressful. For hotels I care about good reviews and a real gym; pool or hot tub would be a plus for the weekend.

Got it. I’ll treat Wednesday arrival as the target if it does not put badge pickup at risk, with Tuesday as the fallback. Are you open to Southwest, Delta, or American if the itinerary is cleaner or cheaper, or should I weight United when comparable?
United is fine when it’s basically tied, but I care more about a simple route and not sitting through some long connection. One short layover is okay; two is not worth it.

For DEN-BNA, the best flight shape is nonstop. Shortlist: 1) United Wed Oct 14 8:05 a.m.-11:33 a.m., nonstop, about $196 main cabin; safest Wednesday option and seat selection is straightforward. 2) Southwest Wed 11:15 a.m.-2:41 p.m., nonstop, about $148 Wanna Get Away; better time of day but less buffer if pickup starts early or lines are long. 3) United Tue 2:10 p.m.-5:36 p.m., nonstop, about $185; best if the agenda later shows a Wednesday morning requirement, but it adds a hotel night. I would not chase the one-stop American or Delta options because they are only modestly cheaper and add connection risk.
That’s helpful. If the pickup ends up mid-afternoon, is the Southwest arrival too cute? I can carry on, but I still have to get from BNA to downtown.

If pickup opens at 2:00 and closes around 5:00, the Southwest flight is tight but not impossible: land 2:41, deplane 2:55, rideshare 25-35 minutes, downtown around 3:30 if everything behaves. A 45-minute delay would start to pinch. The United morning flight gives you lunch, hotel bag drop, and no rush. If you want a low-risk Wednesday arrival, I’d keep United 8:05 as the baseline until the final agenda posts.
Okay. What would Sunday return look like if the spouse weekend happens?

Sunday Oct 18 has a clean afternoon option: United nonstop BNA-DEN 3:35 p.m.-5:24 p.m., about $188 one-way. Southwest has a noon nonstop around $159, and Delta has a one-stop through Atlanta midafternoon for about $171. I’d rank the United return first because it preserves Sunday morning, avoids a connection, and the price gap is small.
Now hotels. The block is convenient, but I don’t want a depressing workshop hotel if we tack on the weekend.

I see three sensible hotel strategies. The block at Renaissance Nashville is the easiest for work: about $249/night before tax, Google rating around 4.5, direct downtown location, fitness center and indoor pool, no hot tub listed, and the remaining block inventory looks like standard rooms. Drury Plaza Hotel Nashville Downtown is a stronger all-around comfort pick: usually $289-$319 that weekend, around 4.7 Google rating, pool, hot tub, fitness room, breakfast and evening snacks, and an 8-10 minute walk to Music City Center. Hyatt Centric Downtown is a nicer-feeling leisure option with a rooftop pool and gym, often around $300-$330, but no hot tub and a longer walk. For pure workshop logistics, Renaissance wins. For the weekend with your husband, Drury is the best value upgrade.
Would you split it or stay put? I hate changing hotels on work trips unless the upside is real.

I’d split only if the extension becomes real. Staying at Renaissance all the way through Sunday avoids a move and keeps every workshop morning simple, but you are paying weekend rates for a room that is mainly convenient. Splitting to Drury for Friday and Saturday nights adds a bag move, but it gives you the hot tub, pool, and gym setup and a more relaxed spouse weekend. If the workshop ends Friday afternoon and he arrives Friday night or Saturday, the move is manageable. If there’s a Saturday morning lab demo, I would rather move Friday evening than check out before the demo.
Can we hold both without creating a cancellation mess? I don’t know his timing yet.

Yes, if both are fully cancellable. I’d hold Renaissance for Wednesday-Friday first, meaning Wednesday and Thursday nights for the certification. Then hold Drury for Friday-Sunday as a backup leisure extension. If you later skip the weekend, cancel Drury and book a Friday or Saturday return. If the agenda forces Tuesday arrival, add Tuesday to Renaissance if the block still allows it.
I probably need Friday night regardless unless there is a late flight home, so maybe the split would start Friday. What about one continuous Drury stay instead of the block?

Continuous Drury Wednesday-Sunday is also viable: more comfortable and no move. Trade-off is about $160-$220 more than using the block for the workshop nights, and it is a longer walk each morning. For a certification where being on time and close to badge pickup matters, I’d use the block for Wednesday and Thursday, then Drury for Friday and Saturday. If you decide Tuesday arrival is needed, add Tuesday at Renaissance and keep the Friday switch.
Good. Don’t book anything prepaid. And for rooms, king is ideal if my husband comes; balcony is nice but not a hill to die on.

Understood. For the hotel holds I’d pick cancellable rates only: Renaissance standard king if it appears, otherwise standard two-queen as a placeholder; Drury deluxe king Friday-Sunday. Balcony availability is limited in that downtown set, so I’d treat it as a bonus rather than the deciding factor.
Give me a working plan I can watch for a few days while the agenda shakes out.

Working Nashville plan: use Wednesday Oct 14 as the target arrival unless the agenda reveals a morning requirement. Flight baseline is United DEN-BNA 8:05 a.m.-11:33 a.m.; Southwest 11:15 a.m.-2:41 p.m. is the cheaper but tighter alternate if pickup is clearly late afternoon. Return baseline for the extension is United BNA-DEN Sunday Oct 18 3:35 p.m.-5:24 p.m. Hotels: hold Renaissance Nashville block for the certification nights because it is closest and well reviewed, then hold Drury Plaza Friday-Sunday as the comfort upgrade if your husband joins. Keep everything cancellable, and revisit once badge pickup and the Saturday plan are confirmed.

messages.content: Agenda posted. Badge pickup is Wednesday 2:00-5:30, welcome at 6:00, sessions Thursday and Friday, and there’s an optional lab demo Saturday 9:00-11:00. My husband can get to Nashville Friday evening if I come home Sunday. The Renaissance block only has two-queen rooms left. Drury has a king and the pool/hot tub/gym. Can you help me choose and lock the flight plan?

This makes Wednesday morning arrival much safer than the cheaper late-morning option. The Southwest 11:15 arrival around 2:41 would work on paper, but one moderate delay crowds badge pickup and hotel check-in. I’d take United 8:05 a.m.-11:33 a.m. from Denver. For the return, the Sunday 3:35 p.m. United nonstop still looks like the cleanest fit after the Saturday demo and a relaxed Sunday morning.
I was hoping not to leave Denver that early, but I don’t want to be sprinting to badge pickup. Is there any true afternoon departure that works?

The true afternoon nonstop gets into Nashville after 5:00, which is too tight for a 5:30 pickup cutoff and a 6:00 welcome. There are one-stop options leaving around noon that arrive around 5:00, but they add a connection and still do not buy much margin. I’d call the 8:05 United the practical choice, not because it is the prettiest time of day, but because it protects the first day.
Fair. Main cabin, not basic. I’ll carry on. If you can request a window, do it, just not an exit row.

Main Cabin on the United nonstop outbound and return, carry-on compatible, window seat request, non-exit row. I’ll keep the seat request separate from the itinerary decision so we don’t give up the cleaner flights just for a seat map.
Now the hotel. Is the split worth the extra hassle if the block only has two queens?

For this agenda, I think the split is worth it. Book Renaissance for Wednesday and Thursday nights only, because it is closest for badge pickup and the two full workshop days. Then move to Drury Friday and Saturday nights, where the king room and better recovery amenities matter for the weekend. Moving Friday after sessions is less disruptive than checking out before the Saturday lab demo, and Drury is still close enough for the 9-11 demo.
What’s the rough cost difference versus just staying at Renaissance through Sunday?

Using the estimates we have: Renaissance all four nights in the two-queen room is about $1,180-$1,250 after taxes and fees. Renaissance Wednesday/Thursday plus Drury Friday/Saturday in a cancellable king is about $1,300-$1,380. So the split likely costs about $120-$150 more, but it improves the weekend room, adds the hot tub, and avoids being stuck with the leftover block room for the leisure part.
That difference is fine. I’ll expense the Wednesday/Thursday part and cover the weekend upgrade personally if needed.

That’s a clean split for receipts: Renaissance under the workshop block for Wednesday/Thursday, Drury as the personal weekend stay for Friday/Saturday. I’d add your husband’s name to the Drury reservation so he can check in or get a key if he arrives before you finish Friday.
Okay, let’s go with that. Can you give me the final set without overexplaining it?

Final Nashville plan to ticket and hold: United Main Cabin DEN-BNA Wednesday Oct 14, 8:05 a.m.-11:33 a.m.; United Main Cabin BNA-DEN Sunday Oct 18, 3:35 p.m.-5:24 p.m.; request non-exit-row window seats. Hotels: Renaissance Nashville workshop block for Wednesday and Thursday nights, cancellable, closest to badge pickup and sessions; Drury Plaza Nashville Downtown for Friday and Saturday nights, cancellable king, with pool, hot tub, and fitness access for the weekend. Keep the Saturday 9-11 lab demo on the calendar, then use Sunday morning as open time before the afternoon return.

messages.content: Before I ticket Nashville, quick wrinkle: Megan can share a ride from BNA if I land between about 4:00 and 4:45 Wednesday. The matching flight is Frontier nonstop 12:55-4:22, about $119 before extras. Is that dumb compared with the United morning flight?
Not dumb, but it changes the risk profile. Are you checking a bag, and is badge pickup still open until 5:30 with the welcome at 6:00?
No checked bag. Carry-on and backpack. Pickup is still 2:00-5:30, welcome at 6:00. I’d pay for a carry-on and probably a seat if Frontier.

Then the comparison is: United 8:05-11:33, about $196 Main Cabin, seat selection included, lots of buffer, but you pay your own ride downtown. Frontier 12:55-4:22, likely $160-$180 once carry-on and seat are added, and Megan’s ride saves another $30-$40. Frontier saves money and transport hassle, but a 45-60 minute delay would put badge pickup and the welcome reception under pressure.
So the real savings are maybe seventy bucks, not the full fare difference.

Right. If this were just a leisure arrival, I’d say take the ride-aligned flight. For a certification start with a fixed pickup window, the United morning nonstop is still the safer buy. The ride is convenient, but it is not enough to give up the buffer unless you are comfortable arriving, dropping bags fast, and possibly missing pickup if the flight slips.
Keep United then. I’ll handle the rideshare and meet her at the hotel later.

Good call. Ticket the United nonstop outbound at 8:05 a.m. and the Sunday 3:35 p.m. nonstop return in Main Cabin, keep the non-exit-row window request, and leave the split hotel plan unchanged: Renaissance Wednesday/Thursday, Drury Friday/Saturday. Megan’s ride can be a backup social plan, not the anchor for the first day.
